serversModal.theServerSVrchatLogin: The server's VRChat login expired, so it isn't logging. Log in again with a new pairing code from the server (its window or admin page).
serversModal.yourKeyLivesOnlyOn: Your key lives only on this device. Servers get the public half, friends' apps lock data for it. If a friend wants to be sure a server isn't faking your key, compare this fingerprint (or put the line below in your VRChat bio: their app then shows your key as confirmed).
serversModal.onlyTheseFriendsGoInto: Only these friends go into your shared friend list, and only time spent between them goes into your activity. Everyone else is left out.
serversModal.onlyThesePeopleCanDownload: Only these people can download what you share here, and only if they joined this server too. Friends who join later get it on your next sync.
serversModal.eachServerSSuggestionOn: Each server's suggestion: on where it recommends encryption, off where it's optional.
serversModal.encryptWhereverTheServerLets: Encrypt wherever the server lets you. Servers that never encrypt start with uploading turned off.
serversModal.donTEncryptWhereThe: Don't encrypt where the server lets you choose (it can then read what you share). Servers that always encrypt still do.
serversModal.runYourOwnDownloadVfm: Run your own: download vfm-server for your device from the releases page and start it; it shows the address.
serversModal.yourCirclesDismissedGroupSuggestions: Your circles, dismissed group suggestions, what you tell friends about people, and per-person notification rules (and settings, if that's on below) go to this server encrypted for your own key only, so the server can't read them. Your other devices pick them up when they sync; edits on both are merged. Your other devices need the same key: Copy key to another device. Age notes stay on each device.
serversModal.friendListYourFriendsNames: Friend list: your friends' names and IDs, so friends see your connections even when VRChat hides mutuals. Activity: how much time pairs of your friends spent in the same instance (from your game logs, live locations and loggers), which makes their group suggestions better. Friend removals: whom you stopped being friends with in the last year, and whether they were in your instance then; your friends see it as a note on that person's profile, so they can ask you about it. Notes about people: only what you chose to tell friends on someone's profile (over 18, probably over 18, or keep your distance); notes saying someone is under 18 never leave your device. Nothing else is sent.
serversModal.whatYouUploadThenDoesn: What you upload then doesn't say who it's for: the server only sees that you shared something, not with whom, and your friends' apps find out themselves whether it's for them. The server can still see whose items each app downloads. Needs encryption. Friends need version 0.12.0 or newer of the app to get it; on older ones it disappears until they update.
serversModal.theServerWatchesYourFriends: The server watches your friends' locations through VRChat's live feed (like this app does while open), around the clock, and counts who is in the same instance as whom. Private and invite-only instances are hidden by VRChat. To pair, it gets your VRChat login (sealed so only that server can open it); logging out of this app keeps it running. Its history comes back to this app signed and encrypted for you.
serversModal.encDefaultWhy: {{why}} A server can still force encryption on or off; then the other side of its switch is greyed out. Changing this resets the switch on every server to the new default.
serversModal.liveWith: Live with {{devices}}: changes and your own notification sounds go across within seconds.
serversModal.peopleValueWithYouFriend_one: {{count}} person shares with you (friend lists show under Shared lists).
serversModal.peopleValueWithYouFriend_other: {{count}} people share with you (friend lists show under Shared lists).
serversModal.shareYourFriendListAnd: Share your friend list and time-together with friends through one or more vfm-servers (yours, a friend's, a public one), and get theirs back. A server on a spare device can also log your friends' instance hopping around the clock. Using more than one server gives redundancy; encrypted uploads keep each server from reading anything.
serversModal.aServerGaveADifferent: A server gave a different key for these people than the one you first got. Usually they reinstalled the app or set up a new device without copying their key; it could also be a server trying to read what you share with them. Until you accept, nothing is sent to or accepted from the new key. Best: ask them for their fingerprint.

ageSettings.forAdultsWhoDRather: For adults who'd rather not have minors on their friend list. A profile's “Age” part shows hints from what the person wrote (bio, pronouns, status, links), your own note, and notes friends shared. VRChat's 18+ badge isn't counted: verified accounts get sold.
ageSettings.linkedPagesOnlyPublicWebsites: Linked pages: only public websites (never your own network), read once and kept for a week. Each site sees your IP address, like when you open it yourself. Also used for guessing friends' time zones.
ageSettings.xShowsProfilesOnlyTo: X shows profiles only to logged-in visitors, so the app asks fxtwitter.com (a free public service) for the bio; that sends them the handle. Deeper reading only follows links to profile sites the app knows (about 50: link pages like Linktree and Carrd, social networks, art sites).
ageSettings.yourNotesAndTheHints: Your notes and the hints stay on this device. Notes saying someone is under 18 are never shared, synced or exported, so this can't turn into a list of minors. Friends can only share “over 18”, “probably over 18” or a neutral “keep your distance”; no note means nothing.

settings.choosePreferTheGraphicsCard: Choose “Prefer the graphics card” if the map is slow or your GPU sits idle; choose “Software” if the window is blank or flickers. Turn on “Show frame rate” in Map options to compare.
